trust_decision.summary: Per file, every storage callback must settle exactly once and any disk write stream's descriptor must be released before its partial file is unlinked, so an aborted request cannot leak a descriptor; this is decided in lib/make-middleware.js's pendingWrites accounting and in storage/disk.js's _handleFile/_removeFile.

landing_point.why: The only place multer opens a disk descriptor: fs.createWriteStream(finalPath) at :40 is preceded by a bare `if (file.stream.destroyed) return` at :38 and followed by file.stream.pipe(outStream) at :44, while the file's only cleanup path (_removeFile, :58-66) just calls fs.unlink and never closes that stream - which is exactly the fd leak the summary names.

fix_sites.entry_point: multer middleware returned by .single()/.array()/.fields()/.any(), mounted on a multipart HTTP route
the three storage-callback branches of the same middleware (aborting, err, success) that decrement pendingWrites
multer.diskStorage() engine used via multer({ storage }) or multer({ dest }), and its _handleFile method callable directly per StorageEngine.md
the same engine's _removeFile, invoked from the abort cleanup at lib/make-middleware.js:146-148

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The other engine never opens a file descriptor, so it can be argued that an fd-leak advisory simply does not cover it ('memoryStorage has nothing to leak'); the same move is available for the untouched abort route, where the middleware deliberately skips waiting for in-flight writes because an aborted request must not be held open.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Abort cleanup must always reach next(err): removeUploadedFiles removes files strictly one after another and calls back only after the last one (lib/remove-uploaded-files.js:7-26), so a _removeFile that waits for a 'close' that never arrives (write stream destroyed with an error, where 'close' is not emitted) hangs the request and leaves the remaining files unremoved; the early fs.unlink path for a file with no tracked stream must stay too.

O6_input_shapes: source file stream already destroyed before _handleFile runs (the guard must call the callback instead of returning)
source destroyed or errored mid-write, where pipe() leaves the write side open and pipeline() destroys it
one file's failure reported twice - stream 'error' event plus storage callback - which must decrement pendingWrites exactly once
write stream already closed vs destroyed with an error so that 'close' is never emitted (Node < 14 emitClose=false); cleanup must settle on 'close' or 'error'

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A storage write that errors drops the file from pendingFiles at the top of the storage callback and never puts it in uploadedFiles, so abort cleanup never calls _removeFile for it and the partially written file created by fs.createWriteStream stays on disk (the 'aborting' branch keeps the file, the 'err' branch does not).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A file whose write failed has nothing valid to remove, and the error branch is about reporting the failure, not cleanup - the disk engine already destroyed its own stream.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same middleware file, one function below the abort cleanup; the file on disk is produced in storage/disk.js:40

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A client abort that lands while the disk engine is still resolving destination/filename leaves the file with no file.path yet, so filesToRemove = pendingFiles.filter(f => f.path) drops it; when the write later fails or lands, nothing unlinks the partial file.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The file has no path yet, so there is nothing to unlink and the engine may not have created anything.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: the async window is in another module's callbacks (storage/disk.js:30-38, crypto.randomBytes at storage/disk.js:6-10) reached through lib/make-middleware.js:296

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Client abort takes abortWithError(err, true) / handleRequestFailure, which skips pendingWrites.onceZero, so cleanup unlinks immediately and the wait for in-flight writes exists only inside the one engine the fix touched; every other engine (including the documented custom-engine route) keeps the original behaviour.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: An aborted request must not be held open waiting for writes, and resource ownership belongs to the storage engine, not the middleware.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~60 lines above the storage callback that reaches the sink

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a memory engine that registers its concat stream and destroys it before releasing the buffer / calling back
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the default engine (index.js:16-18) and implements the identical _handleFile contract documented at StorageEngine.md:3-4, so a maintainer hardening descriptor/callback lifecycles would plausibly add the same guard next door.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third disk-shaped engine copied from the documented template (pipe + createWriteStream + unlink) with its own _removeFile
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The docs publish exactly that code as the template for custom engines, so a sibling engine file that repeats the unfixed pipe/unlink pattern is a realistic addition to our copy.

O9_family: CWE-400 resource exhaustion through CWE-459 incomplete cleanup (file-descriptor leak on aborted/failed uploads)

O10_build.toolchain: npm install; mocha (npm test) with standard for lint; Node >= 10.16.0 per package.json:44-46
O10_build.project_tests: test/orphan-file-cleanup.js and test/async-file-filter-orphan.js already cover abort/orphan cleanup, test/disk-storage.js and test/error-handling.js cover the disk engine; the fix adds four new mocha files under test/ (abort-fd-leak, abort-unlink-after-close, abort-destroyed-stream-callback, pending-writes), none of which exist at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Destroy the write stream right before fs.unlink in _removeFile (and make the destroyed guard call cb) without waiting for 'close', and/or reach for file.stream in cleanup - which still unlinks while the descriptor closes, and file.stream is non-enumerable so it never survives the {...file, ...info} copy.

out_of_scope_notes: The pinned tree already carries abort-cleanup tests citing a different advisory (test/orphan-file-cleanup.js:12, GHSA-3p4h-7m6x-2hcm); used only as context for what the project considers this protection to cover, not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell in this session); the source is four JS files in lib/ and storage/ plus doc/ translations, well under 5 MB, so tiny_repo is asserted from reading the tree.

node_modules is absent from the pinned tree, so busboy/concat-stream internals were not read: the memory-engine consequence (concat callback never fires when the source is destroyed, because pipe does not propagate destroy) is inferred from that well-known pipe/pipeline rule rather than observed.

Whether the fixed pipeline callback fires before or after the fs.WriteStream 'close' was not verified on a running Node, so the WeakMap-keyed-on-file vs {...file, ...info} copy concern is described in O7/O5 rather than claimed as a residual fd leak.
